feature: GitHub and Azure DevOps backlog triage
summary: Replace the GitHub-only triage skill with one `ai-triage` entry point that preserves GitHub behavior and adds safe, complete Azure DevOps Services reports. Each run resolves one scope, reads without remote mutations, and writes a full report only when its inventory is complete.
plain_summary: People can get one complete, ranked backlog report from GitHub or Azure DevOps without changing anything in either service.
gating: Work checkpoints in order. Within a checkpoint, the gates run in order: behavior, then ui, then review. A checkpoint is "passed" only when every gate is "passed" or "n/a". Do not start checkpoint N+1 until checkpoint N has passed.

checkpoints.title: Replace the GitHub-only skill with ai-triage
checkpoints.goal: The branch PRD records the approved scope, one shared Markdown skill preserves the existing GitHub procedure, the retired skill and directory are removed, and Azure targets stop before any remote read.

plain.what: People still get the same GitHub triage instructions from one replacement skill.
plain.why: The public skill must change names without losing its existing provider behavior.
plain.check: Run the skill inventory check and confirm the retired skill directory is absent.

tasks: Sync `.ai-engineering/PRD.html` on this feature branch with the approved decisions from `.ai-engineering/brainstorm.html`.

Create `skills/ai-triage/SKILL.md` as the single shared entry point and move the existing GitHub procedure into `skills/ai-triage/references/github.md`; preserve its issue and pull-request inventories, pagination, per-item analysis, ranking, evidence, report contract, and read-only boundary.

Retire `skills/ai-github-triage/` as part of the same migration, including removal of the empty directory; do not add an alias. Until Azure support is complete, an Azure route must stop before any remote read. Do not add a GitHub runtime helper.
acceptance: The PRD contains the approved single-skill replacement and GitHub-preservation decisions without changing unrelated product scope.
Only `ai-triage` is the public skill name; `skills/ai-github-triage/` is gone, no alias or GitHub runtime helper exists, and an Azure target fails closed before reading.
The shared entry point and GitHub provider reference remain Markdown instructions and preserve the existing GitHub report contract.

checkpoints.title: Prove the GitHub Markdown contract statically
checkpoints.goal: A deterministic static contract test protects the GitHub provider instructions and existing report template without inventing an executable provider runtime.

plain.what: A small check catches missing GitHub inventory and report instructions.
plain.why: The provider is agent-executed Markdown, not a script with a synthetic runtime.
plain.check: Run the static GitHub instruction-contract test.

tasks: Add `tests/triage-github.spec.ts` as a deterministic static instruction-contract check over the GitHub Markdown and existing report template; assert separate issue/PR inventories, complete pagination and counts, per-item analysis, evidence, ranking, read-only rules, report coverage, and no active remote mutation commands. Do not add or expect a GitHub runtime runner or synthetic execution.

Keep the GitHub reference explicit about a closed read-only command allowlist, reject path-qualified executables and shell composition, and state that executable resolution relies on a trusted PATH rather than a sandbox.
acceptance: The static GitHub instruction-contract check verifies separate issue/PR inventories, complete pagination and counts, per-item analysis, evidence, ranking, read-only rules, report-template coverage, and no active remote mutation commands; it does not execute a synthetic provider run.

checkpoints.title: Regenerate and verify the embedded skill payload
checkpoints.goal: Generated assets include the shared skill and GitHub provider reference and no retired skill payload.

plain.what: Installed packages contain the same current skill as the repository.
plain.why: A renamed skill must remain available after packaging.
plain.check: Run the embed-canon, typecheck, and lint gates.

tasks: Regenerate `src/assets.ts` with `bun scripts/gen-assets.ts` and verify the new skill and provider reference are embedded while the retired skill is absent.
Keep the static GitHub contract test type-safe under the project-wide TypeScript check.
acceptance: `bun test tests/embed-canon.spec.ts` proves the new skill and provider reference are embedded and the retired skill payload is absent.
`bun run typecheck` and `bun run lint` pass with the restored locked dependencies.

checkpoints.title: Resolve Azure targets before reading
checkpoints.goal: A deterministic resolver chooses an explicit URL's provider and scope or a unique repository remote, and returns an ambiguity that must be answered before any Azure request.

plain.what: The skill knows which Azure project and board to read, or asks before opening anything.
plain.why: Guessing from the signed-in account could expose the wrong team's private backlog.
plain.check: Try clear and ambiguous URLs and remotes; ambiguous cases must make no read call.

tasks: Add `skills/ai-triage/scripts/resolve-target.mjs` to resolve explicit GitHub or Azure DevOps Services URLs before remotes, and otherwise derive only the provider and project scope established by repository remotes.
Return an explicit needs-answer result when provider, project, team, board or backlog level is ambiguous; have `skills/ai-triage/SKILL.md` ask before reading and retain any answer only for that run.
Require explicit Azure organization and project arguments downstream; reject Azure DevOps Server and never inspect active `az` defaults or add a triage field to `.ai-engineering/config.toml`.
Add separate unit and integration tests using synthetic URLs/remotes and a fake request adapter that proves ambiguous and unsupported targets trigger zero reads.
acceptance: An explicit URL fixes provider and scope even when repository remotes disagree.
Without a URL, only one unambiguous remote determines provider/project; missing or conflicting provider, project or board information asks before any read.
Azure Services targets carry explicit organization and project values; no active Azure CLI default or persisted config field supplies scope.
Synthetic tests cover GitHub and Azure URLs, unique and conflicting remotes, missing board selection, unsupported Azure Server, and zero reads on ambiguity.

checkpoints.title: Collect a complete read-only Azure backlog
checkpoints.goal: The selected Azure backlog level yields a complete, normalized inventory of nonterminal work items using process-aware state categories, bounded batch reads and a provable completion condition; otherwise collection fails closed.

plain.what: The report receives every eligible item from one board, with related parents or children only as context.
plain.why: A capped or guessed list could hide work and make the ranking misleading.
plain.check: Synthetic large backlogs must finish completely or report failure, never a smaller complete-looking list.

tasks: Add `skills/ai-triage/scripts/collect-azure.mjs` and `skills/ai-triage/references/azure-devops.md` for Azure DevOps Services only; use explicit organization/project scope and one selected board/backlog level per run.

Discover work-item types and their process state categories; include every nonterminal category without hard-coded state names, and fetch parent/child links only for context without widening the inventory.

Define and enforce this default-deny `az devops invoke` allowlist with explicit `--organization`, project/team route parameters and API version: GET `/{project}/{team}/_apis/work/backlogs`; GET `/{project}/{team}/_apis/work/backlogs/{backlogId}/workItems`; GET `/{project}/_apis/wit/workitemtypes`; GET `/{project}/_apis/wit/workitemtypes/{type}/states`; POST `/{project}/_apis/wit/workitemsbatch`. Verify each route before implementation; add no other route/method pair without a documented read need and a pinned test.

Use the selected backlog's own work-items endpoint to preserve exact board membership; do not substitute flat-only `az boards query` or WIQL whose parity with backlog membership is unproven. Allow POST only for the listed read-only batch endpoint, require explicit organization/project arguments, and cap each batch at 200 IDs.

Use the backlog level's documented `workItemCountLimit` as a fail-closed boundary: if the limit is absent/unknown or the returned item count reaches it, stop without a report rather than claim completeness. Do not invent continuation tokens or keyset pagination absent documented backlog-equivalent semantics.

Test full inventory below the configured boundary, boundary/unknown cap failure, missing state metadata, API/auth errors and batches above 200 with sanitized synthetic fixtures in separate unit/integration suites.
acceptance: The synthetic inventory contains every and only nonterminal item for the selected process-aware backlog level; parent/child context never adds inventory rows.

Every request matches an allowlisted method and route, carries explicit organization/project scope, and batch requests contain at most 200 IDs; no mutation-capable route or unbounded `invoke` is emitted.
The selected backlog endpoint returns fewer items than its known `workItemCountLimit`; an unknown limit or a count at/over the cap fails rather than returning a complete flag.
Unknown process state categories, incomplete pagination, authentication failures and any non-allowlisted call stop collection without producing a report.
All Azure tests use synthetic fixtures; this checkpoint makes no tenant or authentication query.

checkpoints.title: Render safe Azure content in the shared shell
checkpoints.goal: A complete synthetic Azure inventory renders Azure-specific sections in the shared artifact shell. Untrusted HTML is inert, credential-like URL values are checked raw and decoded, unsafe links are omitted, and safe HTTPS links remain usable.

plain.what: People can read the full Azure backlog in a page that keeps its details safe.
plain.why: Untrusted work-item content or links must not execute or expose credential-like values.
plain.check: Render a synthetic Azure report and confirm its provider sections and safe links appear while hostile content stays inert.

tasks: Add `skills/ai-triage/scripts/render-report.mjs` and wire the shared router, Azure collector and report writer to `.ai-engineering/triage.html` only after routing and inventory completeness pass.

Reuse the existing shell and artifact design in `templates/triage.html.tpl`; render Azure-specific scope, ranked work, work-item types/states, related context and method sections rather than GitHub-only issue/PR sections.
Preserve per-item analysis for the complete inventory with no more than five analysts in flight, and show every item or an explicit `UNASSESSED` status instead of dropping unreviewed items.

Escape untrusted Azure fields before rendering HTML text or attributes; check raw and safely decoded URL components for credential-like values, omit unsafe or malformed links, and keep valid safe HTTPS links.

Use separate synthetic unit and integration coverage in `tests/triage-report.unit.spec.ts` and `tests/triage-report.integration.spec.ts` for escaping, URL safety, complete rows/counts/linkages, Azure-specific shared-shell sections, and bounded analysis.
acceptance: A synthetic full run writes a complete HTML report to `.ai-engineering/triage.html` with Azure-specific sections inside the existing shared shell.
Every inventoried work item and its expected details/linkage is represented; report totals agree with inventory totals and related parent/child context does not inflate them.

Untrusted fields render as inert text; credential-like URL values are rejected in raw and decoded forms, unsafe links are omitted, safe HTTPS links remain clickable, and no authentication value is rendered.
Shared-shell/layout gates and the separate synthetic unit/integration tests pass without reading or storing private Azure data.

findings: F3/P1: bearer-style credentials in URL fragments may survive href validation.
F4/P1: credential-shaped backlogName metadata may render without redaction.
F5/P2: unsafe evidence/relationship URLs currently fail the report instead of falling back to plain safe text.

checkpoints.title: Preserve the previous report on write failures
checkpoints.simple: Keep the last report if saving fails
checkpoints.goal: The report writer replaces the report atomically after a successful temporary write, and partial-write or replacement failures preserve the previous report byte-for-byte while cleaning up only temporary files it owns.

plain.what: A failed save keeps the last good report in place.
plain.why: A partial or failed replacement must never destroy the report people already have.
plain.check: Inject write and replacement failures and confirm the previous bytes remain unchanged.

tasks: Keep report publication behind a temporary-file write followed by replacement; track temporary-file ownership so cleanup never removes another file.

Use synthetic integration coverage in `tests/triage-report.integration.spec.ts` to inject partial temporary-write and replacement errors through the real writer, verify a successful replacement publishes the complete report, and assert previous bytes and owned-temp cleanup on failures.
acceptance: Successful publication replaces the report with the complete rendered bytes.
Injected partial-write and replacement failures leave the previous report byte-for-byte unchanged.
Failure cleanup removes only an owned temporary file; no private Azure data or live report is used.

checkpoints.title: Close documentation and verify the full feature
checkpoints.goal: Current documentation names only `ai-triage`, generated assets include the final shared and provider-specific procedures, and the complete GitHub/Azure suite and project gates pass without a private live report in the changes.

plain.what: People can find the new skill and understand what it reads and what it never changes.
plain.why: Outdated instructions could send people to a removed skill or imply Azure can be modified.
plain.check: Read the skill summary and run every project check before the feature is handed off.

tasks: Update the current skill listing in `README.md`, add the user-facing replacement/Azure Services entry to `CHANGELOG.md`, and update `FILEMAP.md` for the new skill structure; retain historical release entries as history.

Review `skills/ai-triage/SKILL.md` and provider references for one entry point, no alias, exact read-only Azure allowlist, explicit scope, per-run ambiguity answers, one-level inventory, five-agent cap, failure behavior and no configuration field.
Run `bun scripts/gen-assets.ts`, then verify `src/assets.ts` and embedded canon contain only the current skill paths.

Run the full suite and required project gates; optionally perform a live Azure smoke read only if separately authorized, using only allowlisted read calls, keeping raw/private output out of Git and never committing or pushing the live report.
acceptance: README and current instructions refer to `ai-triage`, not a separate `ai-github-triage` alias; changelog and file map match the final shipped structure.
The final embedded payload has the replacement skill and provider procedures and no retired skill folder.
`bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, `bun test`, and `bun test tests/arch.spec.ts` all pass.
Automated checks use synthetic data only; no live private report or raw backlog output is added to Git, committed or pushed.

assumptions: Azure support means Azure DevOps Services only, not Azure DevOps Server. [Approved brainstorm, sections 8 and 11]

An explicit URL fixes provider and scope; repository remotes may resolve only what they identify, and ambiguous provider, project or board choices are asked per run. [Approved brainstorm, sections 6 and 8]

One Azure run inventories one selected backlog level, while parents and children are context only; each item keeps the GitHub analysis contract with at most five analysts in flight. [Approved feature decisions and existing GitHub procedure]
Azure state names vary by process, so terminal status is derived from discovered state categories rather than fixed names. [Approved feature decisions]

`az devops invoke` resolves area/resource names through read-only service metadata calls; the collector must still constrain each final method/route pair, reject mutations, and pass explicit scope. [Official CLI extension research, no tenant call]
If state discovery or pagination cannot prove a complete inventory, collection stops and the existing report stays unchanged. [Approved fail-closed and preserve-previous-report decisions]
Automated fixtures contain synthetic data only; a private real report is local output and never a committed or pushed artifact. [Approved brainstorm, sections 5 and 8]
The existing Bun toolchain is sufficient; no new dependency is needed unless implementation proves a required capability is absent. [AGENTS.md Project config and user instruction]
GitHub provider procedures are agent-executed Markdown; their command contract is tested statically, not with a synthetic runtime.

GitHub and Azure CLI command rules require bare allowlisted executable names, no path prefixes, environment assignments, or shell wrappers. This protects command shape but assumes the user's PATH is trusted; it is not an executable-identity sandbox. [Human circuit-breaker decision]
notes: Original baseline note: the feature PRD was missing before its ai-triage scope was added; checkpoint 1 still syncs the branch PRD from the approved brainstorm without changing the primary checkout.

Microsoft documents no continuation token for backlog-level workItems or WIQL, and no documented WIQL mapping proves parity with backlog membership. Use the backlog-level endpoint and fail closed at an unknown/reached workItemCountLimit; support beyond that boundary requires a documented equivalent paging mechanism.
No Azure tenant or authentication query is part of planning or automated verification. A later live smoke read is optional and requires separate authorization; raw output stays out of Git.
No remote Azure mutation, multi-board aggregation, Azure DevOps Server support, persistent board configuration, commit or push of a live private report is in scope.

Superseded checkpoint 1 attempt 1: `bun test tests/triage-github.spec.ts` failed before tests ran because it imported `skills/ai-triage/scripts/github.mjs`, which is outside the approved Markdown-skill design. The plan was corrected to a static Markdown instruction-contract test; lesson L31 says not to invent a runtime for an agent-executed procedure.

Superseded checkpoint 1 attempt 2: `bun test tests/skills.spec.ts` found the empty retired `skills/ai-github-triage/` directory after the skill file was renamed. Only that empty directory was removed; the targeted test then passed (19 passed) with no tracked file changes. Lesson L32 says retirement checks include directory presence.

Superseded checkpoint 1 attempt 3: `bun run typecheck` exited 127 because `oxlint` was absent. `bun install --frozen-lockfile` restored dependencies without manifest or lock changes; `oxlint` 1.80.0 became available and typecheck exited 0 with warnings. Lesson L33 says to restore locked dependencies before typecheck.
The three replacement checkpoints are pending with behavior/review gates reset; the historical failures and fixes above are retained as planning notes, not current gate results.
Human resumed checkpoint 2 with the trusted-PATH boundary after review circuit breaker F11; require bare command names and document that the contract is not a sandbox.

Checkpoint 6 re-plan history (new gates are pending; these are historical outcomes): behavior passed after two attempts. The behavior failure was TS2769 from an unnarrowed optional recorded write; it was fixed by narrowing before `writeFile` (L51: narrow indexed values before typed use). Round 1 failed on shell metadata that HTML-escaped but did not redact credential-shaped values and missing injected write-failure coverage; fixes used shared redact-then-escape handling and added partial-write/replacement tests with temporary-file ownership tracking. Round 2 failed because token-shaped project values appeared in work-item URLs; the fix rejected credential-shaped URL values and fell back to safe IDs, while write-preservation coverage was resolved. Round 3 failed because percent-encoded credential-like organization/project values bypassed raw-only shell redaction; the fix checked encoded values in metadata, while write-failure coverage remained resolved. Round 4 passed after checking raw and decoded URL components, omitting unsafe links while retaining safe HTTPS links; synthetic unit/integration tests passed (6/6 and 11/11). L52 lesson: validate untrusted URL values before encoding or rendering them. Keep the approved trusted-PATH and privacy decisions unchanged: no Azure tenant, real report, commit, or push.
